updates.text: Security: Paris, Nord and Nice curfew orders posted with hours and streets; Money: insurance claim window extended from five to thirty days

title: Count the curfew hours, not the speech.

pages.title: A curfew is a timetable, and a timetable can be checked

a-curfew-is-a-timetable-and-a-timetable-.title: A curfew is a timetable, and a timetable can be checked
a-curfew-is-a-timetable-and-a-timetable-.dek: France moved from Sunday's list of meetings to Monday's local curfews, an interior minister kept in post, and a bond market that has already priced the night. Order is measured in hours and invoices, not adjectives.
a-curfew-is-a-timetable-and-a-timetable-.text: This morning’s edition left France with a list of meetings. By Monday afternoon the list had grown teeth. After an emergency meeting with top officials, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he had instructed prefects to impose “very limited” and “localized” curfews where needed, and dismissed the idea of putting all of Paris under one [1][4]. Marseille had already banned most public gatherings for Monday [1]. That is not a slogan. It is a set of hours on a notice, with a start time, an end time and a map. You can check whether it was posted, whether it was kept, and whether the streets were quieter when it ended. The numbers that accompanied the timetable are ugly and specific. The interior ministry counted nearly 2,400 arrests and almost 1,000 police officers and firefighters injured over the weekend of protest and riot; more than half a million people had taken part in the marches, most of them peacefully [1]. Lecornu put the tally of looted or vandalized businesses at about 3,000 [1]. Limoges lost the roof and spire of its nineteenth-century town hall to fire; city halls in Marseille, Lille and Angers were broken into; a tourist office burned in Lyon [1]. The prime minister called it a “miracle” that nobody was killed [1]. Miracles are not a security policy. Counts are. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the police had “lost control” in some cities and that there had been a “lack of anticipation” [2]. He tendered his resignation. President Emmanuel Macron refused it, citing the need to keep a chain of command, and instructed him to put new operational methods in place as quickly as possible and to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence [2]. Keeping the minister is a decision about continuity. Ordering new methods is a decision about paperwork. Both matter. Only the second produces a document you can read later. Markets did not wait for the document. Paris blue chips fell about 1.4% in morning trade; French banks and rate-sensitive property names led the drop; the spread between French and German ten-year yields widened to about 145 basis points, and the ten-year French yield jumped more than ten basis points toward 4.89% [3]. Carrefour’s chief executive said fifty of the chain’s stores had been looted, with repair costs expected above €10 million [3]. That is the quiet print of a riot: not the video of a burning roof, but an invoice and a yield. The constructive reading is not that France is finished. It is that order is machinery. Prefects, curfew hours, gathering bans, arrest tallies, after-action reviews and a budget line for substitute teachers are all boring objects. Boring objects are how you keep the next Saturday from looking like the last one. Macron blamed “troublemakers from far-left fringe groups” for the violence while acknowledging the cost-of-living and school grievances of the peaceful marchers [1]. Separate the grievances from the looting, answer the first with payroll and classrooms, and answer the second with courts and timed restrictions. That is the republic doing its dull work. What to watch tonight is not another speech. It is whether the curfew notices appear with clear hours, whether the after-action review is commissioned with a date attached, and whether the bond market, which has already written its own comment on the weekend, sees anything that looks like a plan rather than a podium. A timetable you can check is a promise you can keep. A speech you can only clap for is not.

macrons-gulf-hours-are-an-energy-invoice.title: Macron's Gulf hours are an energy invoice with a reception line
macrons-gulf-hours-are-an-energy-invoice.dek: Kuwait and Abu Dhabi on Monday, Bahrain and Qatar next: the Élysée framed the tour as fuel security and Hormuz navigation while France counted burned shops at home.
macrons-gulf-hours-are-an-energy-invoice.text: Emmanuel Macron opened a three-day Gulf tour on Monday in Kuwait, then Abu Dhabi, with Bahrain and Qatar still to come [1]. The Élysée’s own framing was blunt: promote stability and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, and “securing and diversifying our energy supplies” to limit the crisis’s impact on daily life in France [1]. TotalEnergies and Engie chiefs travelled with him; Kuwait saw a defence-and-AI agreement including a Kuwait Airways fleet renewal with Airbus [1]. The optics are harsh because the domestic print is harsher. He left hours after promising the trip would help secure fuel, and after a weekend that left about 3,000 businesses looted or vandalized and nearly 2,400 people arrested [2][1]. Critics called the schedule tone-deaf [2]. That criticism does not cancel the logistics. France’s fuel and gas bill is partly written in Gulf barrels and LNG cargoes; a president who refuses to talk about routes and volumes leaves the invoice to the tanker market alone. The constructive test is narrow. Did any stop produce a dated commitment on volumes, routes or insurance that a household might eventually feel at the pump? A reception line is not a cargo. A cargo with a date is.

kuwait-airways-and-the-airbus-line.title: Kuwait Airways and the Airbus line
kuwait-airways-and-the-airbus-line.dek: Macron's first Gulf stop produced a fleet-renewal partnership, not only a reception.
kuwait-airways-and-the-airbus-line.text: In Kuwait City on Monday, Airbus sales executive Benoit de Saint Exupéry and the Kuwait Investment Authority’s Sheikh Saud Salem Abdulaziz Al Sabah signed a partnership that includes renewing the Kuwait Airways fleet [1]. Defence and AI agreements accompanied the visit; TotalEnergies and Engie chiefs travelled onward with Macron toward a Franco-Emirati business summit [1]. Receptions are easy to film. Fleet renewals are invoices with delivery slots. Prefer the second when judging whether a tour changed anything.

hormuz-coalition-still-waiting.title: The Hormuz coalition is still waiting on politics
hormuz-coalition-still-waiting.dek: France and the UK offered a maritime coalition in April. The National notes it still needs a US–Iran political agreement.
hormuz-coalition-still-waiting.text: Macron’s joint offer with the UK in April to launch an international maritime coalition to defend ships in the Strait of Hormuz “awaits a political agreement between the US and Iran,” The National reported alongside Monday’s tour [1]. The Élysée still frames the trip as work for stability and freedom of navigation [1]. An offer without an agreement is a podium with an empty berth. Watch for a dated activation, not another adjective.

paris-priced-the-riot-wiesbaden-printed-.title: Paris priced the riot; Wiesbaden printed the backlog
paris-priced-the-riot-wiesbaden-printed-.dek: French banks and the CAC led Europe lower while Destatis quietly reported another month of manufacturing orders on the books. Two prints, one day.
paris-priced-the-riot-wiesbaden-printed-.text: The screen that moved Europe on Monday was not a factory floor. Paris blue chips fell about 1.4%; BNP Paribas, Société Générale and Crédit Agricole dropped around 2.5%; LVMH lost 2.2% after stores were looted; Carrefour fell 1.8% after its chief executive said fifty of its shops had been ransacked [1]. The pan-European STOXX 600 was down about 0.8% by mid-morning [2]. That is how markets price a weekend of burned town halls: through banks, landlords and retailers with glass on the pavement. Across the Atlantic the story was the opposite of Friday’s AI scare. Chip and AI names led a rebound; the S&P 500 was up about half a percent in early US trade, with Brent off about 1.6% to around $108, which helped keep yields in check [4]. Earnings from Meta, Tesla and several chipmakers land later this week [2][4]. Investors will want free cash flow, not another capital-expenditure slide. The quiet German print cut across both moods. Destatis reported that the real stock of manufacturing orders rose 0.5% in August on July, seasonally and calendar adjusted, and stood 10.7% above a year earlier [3]. The range of the backlog was unchanged at 9.0 months [3]. Machinery, other transport equipment and computers/electronics lifted the total; cars subtracted a little [3]. A backlog is not a boom. It is work already sold and not yet shipped — the opposite of a riot video, and closer to how a winter is paid for. When the riot and the backlog share a Monday, favour the one with a delivery date.

carrefour-fifty-stores-ten-million-euros.title: Carrefour: fifty stores, more than €10 million
carrefour-fifty-stores-ten-million-euros.dek: The retailer's chief executive put a repair bill on the riot. Banks and luxury names took the index down with it.
carrefour-fifty-stores-ten-million-euros.text: Alexandre Bompard said fifty Carrefour stores had been looted during the protests, with repair work expected to cost more than €10 million [1]. The share fell about 1.8% in the same session that took Société Générale down about 2.7% and LVMH about 2.2% after luxury stores were looted [1]. A national index move is abstract. A named store count and a repair envelope are how a riot enters the accounts department.

destatis-nine-months-of-work-on-the-book.title: Destatis: nine months of work still on the books
destatis-nine-months-of-work-on-the-book.dek: August's order stock rose 0.5% on the month. The range stayed at 9.0 months. Cars subtracted; machines and electronics added.
destatis-nine-months-of-work-on-the-book.text: Press release No. 371 of 19 October: real manufacturing order stock +0.5% on July after seasonal and calendar adjustment, +10.7% on August 2025, range unchanged at 9.0 months [1]. Capital-goods producers still show 12.6 months of work; intermediate goods 4.6; consumer goods 4.3 [1]. Automotive stock fell 0.4% on the month; computers, electronics and optical products rose 1.4% [1]. A backlog is the opposite of a protest video — dull, dated, and already sold.

the-annex-what-mondays-refusal-actually-.title: The Annex: what Monday's refusal actually instructed
the-annex-what-mondays-refusal-actually-.dek: Nuñez offered to go. Macron kept him. The Élysée statement is shorter than the argument about it, and it names the deliverables.
the-annex-what-mondays-refusal-actually-.text: The annex this evening is the Élysée’s Monday statement on Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, as reported by Reuters [1]. What Nuñez said. The police “lost control” in some cities. There had been a “lack of anticipation.” He tendered his resignation “because I felt responsible for everything that happened” [1]. What Macron refused. Continuity of command for law enforcement “at this time.” The resignation was declined [1]. What Macron ordered instead. Two deliverables, not one adjective. First: “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence.” Second: “put in place new operational methods for security forces” as quickly as possible, including approaches to deal with looters [1]. What sits beside it. Lecornu’s instruction to prefects for localized curfews [2]. Sunday’s presidential address promising a prime-ministerial round table this week on schools and cost of living [3]. Opposition calls for Nuñez to be sacked [1]. The reading. A resignation refused without instructions is theatre. A resignation refused with two written tasks is a work order. Hold the ministry to the work order: a dated review, and operational methods that can be explained without a podium.

lecornu-rejected-a-paris-wide-curfew.title: Lecornu rejected a Paris-wide curfew
lecornu-rejected-a-paris-wide-curfew.dek: Localized and limited, he said — and dismissed putting the whole capital under one clock.
lecornu-rejected-a-paris-wide-curfew.text: After the crisis meeting, Sébastien Lecornu said he had asked some local authorities to introduce curfews but dismissed putting all of Paris under such a measure [1]. AP reported his instruction to prefects for “very limited” and “localized” curfews [2]. That distinction matters. A national emergency declaration was urged by some on the right; Macron stopped short [1]. The tool chosen is the prefecture’s timed order, which can be checked street by street. Hold each prefect to the notice they actually post.

the-round-table-still-has-no-numbers.title: The round table still has no numbers
the-round-table-still-has-no-numbers.dek: Sunday promised pupils, teachers and unions at one table this week. Monday's security work did not yet publish the timetable of hires.
the-round-table-still-has-no-numbers.text: Macron’s Sunday address asked the prime minister to bring pupils, students, teachers, unions, employers and local authorities to one table for concrete proposals this week [1]. The government had already promised 3,000 more substitute teachers and scrapped some planned university fee rises [2]. Security swallowed Monday’s headlines. The school grievance that started the autumn still needs a dated roster. A round table without numbers is a meeting; a roster with start dates is a policy.

podium-vs-print-the-ai-couple-and-the-re.title: Podium vs Print: the AI couple and the real invoice
podium-vs-print-the-ai-couple-and-the-re.dek: An image of an elderly pair stripped in the street ran ahead of the riot debate. CheckNews and SynthID said it was synthetic. Fifty Carrefour stores were not.
podium-vs-print-the-ai-couple-and-the-re.text: The podium. Amid real fires and real arrests, an image of an elderly couple supposedly left in underwear after a robbery near Place de la République spread as proof of the night [1]. It looked like the weekend. That was the point. The print. Fact-checkers at Libération’s CheckNews, and detection tools including Google’s SynthID, flagged the image as AI-generated or heavily edited — missing fingers, merged figures, watermarks [1]. Separate from that fiction, Carrefour’s chief executive said fifty of the chain’s stores had been looted, with repairs expected to cost more than €10 million [2]. Nearly 2,400 people were arrested; about 3,000 businesses were looted or vandalized [3]. Those figures do not need a generator. The gap. A synthetic image borrows the authority of a photograph and spends it before the receipt arrives. The constructive habit is small and stubborn: when a picture arrives hotter than the official count, ask who measured the glass. The couple image failed that test. The Carrefour invoice did not. Verdict. The weekend was violent enough without inventions. Prefer the store tally, the arrest sheet and the curfew notice to any image that cannot survive a finger count.

a-picture-that-failed-the-finger-count.title: A picture that failed the finger count
a-picture-that-failed-the-finger-count.dek: CheckNews and SynthID flagged the viral elderly-couple image. The weekend's real tallies did not need it.
a-picture-that-failed-the-finger-count.text: An image of an elderly couple allegedly stripped after a robbery near Place de la République spread through the riot debate; Libération’s CheckNews and Google’s SynthID flagged AI artefacts — missing fingers, merged figures [1]. Real counts already existed: nearly 2,400 arrests, about 3,000 businesses damaged, almost 1,000 officers and firefighters injured [2]. Synthetic horror borrows urgency from real glass. The constructive habit is to demand the official tally before the generated frame sets the mood.

limoges-mayor-called-it-an-attack-on-the.title: Limoges's mayor called it an attack on the republic
limoges-mayor-called-it-an-attack-on-the.dek: Guillaume Guérin linked the burned town hall to the state itself. That is rhetoric — and also a claim about what a municipal building is for.
limoges-mayor-called-it-an-attack-on-the.text: After flames took the roof and spire of Limoges’s nineteenth-century town hall, Mayor Guillaume Guérin wrote that to attack the building was to attack the republic [1]. Strong words. They also name a function: a town hall is where permits, civil status and council votes live. Rebuilding it is not nostalgia; it is restoring a counter where ordinary life is stamped. Watch the reconstruction timetable as closely as the anniversary speeches.

gas-climbed-while-oil-slipped.title: Gas climbed while oil slipped — heating oil barely noticed
gas-climbed-while-oil-slipped.dek: Brent eased toward $108 on the Russia waiver. European gas near €89/MWh still worried about LNG and storage. Gasoil kept German heating-oil quotes almost flat.
gas-climbed-while-oil-slipped.text: Oil and gas told different stories on Monday. Brent fell about 1.5–1.6% toward the high-$107s / low-$108s as traders weighed the US waiver on new Russia-related duties; WTI was softer too [1][3]. European natural gas, by contrast, was quoted near €88.92/MWh, up about 1.6%, on worries about LNG from the Gulf and the need to refill storage before winter [1]. EU underground storage was recently reported around 74.5% full on AGSI+-based trackers — well below the policy ambition of 90% by early winter [4][1]. German heating-oil buyers felt almost none of the crude dip. HeizOel24 noted Brent near $108.71 at midday, about a dollar below Friday’s close, while gasoil — the exchange foundation for heating oil and diesel — was still about $1,447.50 a tonne, above Friday afternoon’s $1,413, having only partly given back Friday night’s spike [2]. That is why quotes in Germany and Austria barely moved [2]. Desk arithmetic, labelled as such: a barrel can fall while a litre of heating oil does not, if the refined contract that dealers hedge with stays elevated. Read gasoil and AGSI before you celebrate a Brent screen.

gasoil-still-above-fridays-afternoon.title: Gasoil still above Friday afternoon
gasoil-still-above-fridays-afternoon.dek: $1,447.50 a tonne against $1,413: the wedge that kept heating-oil quotes almost flat while Brent eased.
gasoil-still-above-fridays-afternoon.text: HeizOel24’s Monday midday note put ICE gasoil at about $1,447.50 a tonne, still above Friday afternoon’s $1,413, even as Brent slipped to about $108.71 [1]. Heating-oil dealers hedge with gasoil, not with a Brent screenshot. That is why German and Austrian household quotes barely moved [1]. Until the refined contract gives back the spike, a cheaper barrel is a headline without a delivery discount.

european-gas-near-eighty-nine.title: European gas near €89 while oil retreated
european-gas-near-eighty-nine.dek: TTF-linked quotes around €88.92/MWh rose on LNG and storage worries even as Brent softened.
european-gas-near-eighty-nine.text: European gas was quoted near €88.92/MWh on Monday, up about 1.6%, on concerns about Gulf LNG and the need to refill storage [1]. EU storage trackers citing AGSI+ recently showed fills around 74.5%, against a policy ambition of 90% in the early-winter window [1][2]. Oil can fall on a sanctions waiver while gas rises on a winter inventory gap. Households that heat with gas feel the second story first.

frances-ten-year-yield-wrote-the-evening.title: France's ten-year yield wrote the evening comment
frances-ten-year-yield-wrote-the-evening.dek: OATs jumped more than ten basis points toward 4.89%; the premium over Bunds widened to about 145 basis points. The euro hovered near $1.12. That is the market's after-action report.
frances-ten-year-yield-wrote-the-evening.text: French ten-year yields rose more than ten basis points on Monday, trading close to 4.89%, while the spread over German Bunds widened to about 145 basis points — the highest in two weeks on that report [1]. Other desks saw the French ten-year near 4.875% with Bunds around 3.43% [3]. The euro slipped toward $1.122 [1][3]. None of those figures require a press conference. The economic backdrop was already tight: fiscal strain, a 2027 presidential race, and a minority government that still has to pass a budget and a deficit path [2]. Weekend unrest layered political risk on top. Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid called it “another layer of political risk for markets” [1]. French bank shares, which feel sovereign stress quickly, fell harder than the index [1][3]. The constructive reading is institutional, not fatalistic. Spreads widen when buyers demand compensation for uncertainty; they narrow when the uncertainty is reduced by dated plans — curfew hours, operational reviews, budget arithmetic. The screen is already doing the homework. The government still has to hand in its own.

oat-bund-at-about-one-forty-five.title: OAT–Bund at about 145 basis points
oat-bund-at-about-one-forty-five.dek: French ten-years toward 4.89%; the premium over Germany the widest in two weeks on the Dow Jones morning print.
oat-bund-at-about-one-forty-five.text: Morning reports put the French–German ten-year spread near 145 basis points and the French ten-year close to 4.89% after a jump of more than ten basis points [1]. A later Reuters wrap had France at about 4.875% and Germany at about 3.428% [2]. Small differences between wires are normal intraday noise. The direction is not: France paid more to borrow on Monday because politics and the street added risk to an already strained fiscal story. Spreads are the homework markets set for governments.

five-days-became-thirty.title: Five days became thirty: the claim form moved first
five-days-became-thirty.dek: Before anyone named a sum, the state changed the insurance clock. For a looted shop, the deadline matters more than an adjective.
five-days-became-thirty.text: The most useful thing a minister said on Monday was a number of days. Serge Papin, the minister for small businesses, said the window for declaring damage to insurers would go from five days to thirty [1]. Five days is not long when your shutters are broken and your stock is gone. Thirty days gives you time to count it properly. The rest of the toolkit is administrative too. The government said at least 3,000 businesses had been damaged or looted over the weekend, and that they could get short-time working support from Tuesday plus a dedicated support fund [1]. Françoise Gatel, the minister for local authorities, announced an exceptional fund to rebuild destroyed public buildings and a single point of contact at each prefecture, but gave no amount [1]. Casino’s chief executive said nearly 50 of the group’s stores had been attacked and 32 looted, and that none of its independent franchisees would go bankrupt [1]. None of this is a cheque yet. When a fund comes without an amount, it is still only an announcement. The amount, the eligibility rules and how fast money is paid out are the parts to watch. Until then, the thirty days is what has actually changed for a shopkeeper.

the-euro-hovered-near-one-twelve.title: The euro hovered near $1.12
the-euro-hovered-near-one-twelve.dek: A soft single currency on French stress, not a collapse. Watch the OAT spread more than the second decimal on EURUSD.
the-euro-hovered-near-one-twelve.text: The euro weakened about 0.1% to roughly $1.1224 in morning European trade on the Dow Jones report [1]; HeizOel24 had it near $1.12 at midday [2]. That is soft, not a regime change. Imported dollar oil gets a little dearer in euro terms when the single currency slips — another reason a Brent dip may not reach a German tank. Prefer the OAT–Bund spread as the day’s stress gauge.

ordinary-ledger-the-litre-that-ignored-t.title: Ordinary Ledger: the litre that ignored the barrel
ordinary-ledger-the-litre-that-ignored-t.dek: Brent fell about a dollar. German and Austrian heating-oil quotes barely budged, because gasoil had not finished giving back Friday's jump. Your dealer still quotes your postcode.
ordinary-ledger-the-litre-that-ignored-t.text: Monday’s ordinary ledger is short on purpose. Screen. Brent at midday about $108.71, roughly a dollar below Friday’s close, after the US waived new Graham Act duties on Russia-related energy trade [1]. WTI near $101.26 [1]. Hedge. Gasoil, the contract heating-oil dealers watch, about $1,447.50 a tonne — still above Friday afternoon’s $1,413 — so most of Friday night’s spike was still in the refined print [1]. Doorstep. HeizOel24: heating-oil prices in Germany and Austria “nearly unchanged”; Switzerland a bit softer [1]. Sunday night’s tanke-günstig national average for a 2,000-litre order was €177.59 per 100 litres [2]; do not assume Monday erased that. Desk arithmetic (labelled). If Brent falls one dollar and gasoil does not, a 2,000-litre household order should not be expected to fall in lockstep. The binding number remains the written quote for your postcode. Nothing here is advice to buy, wait or switch. It is a reminder that the barrel and the invoice are different documents.

fifty-carrefour-tickets-on-one-chain.title: Fifty Carrefour tickets on one chain
fifty-carrefour-tickets-on-one-chain.dek: Looting is often filmed as chaos. A chief executive's store count turns it into a repair schedule.
fifty-carrefour-tickets-on-one-chain.text: Fifty Carrefour stores looted; more than €10 million expected in repairs [1]. For staff and shoppers those are closed aisles, overtime, and a wait for the glazier. National politics will argue about who is to blame. Ordinary life starts again when the till turns on. That is why a named store count belongs in this desk as much as in markets.

louvre-closed-after-a-blockade-threat.title: The Louvre closed after a blockade threat
louvre-closed-after-a-blockade-threat.dek: A museum shuttered is a tourism invoice and a public-order footnote on the same day.
louvre-closed-after-a-blockade-threat.text: The Louvre said it was closed after protesters announced a blockade of the site [1]. Ticket holders, staff rotas and nearby cafés feel that decision before any manifesto does. Reopening notices are the constructive print to watch — dated, boring, and more useful than another aerial of smoke.

the-rebound-is-a-calendar-not-a-verdict.title: The rebound is a calendar, not a verdict
the-rebound-is-a-calendar-not-a-verdict.dek: AI and chip shares bounced as Meta, Tesla and several semiconductor names prepare to report. Friday's sell-off asked about debt-funded buildout; this week's prints have to answer with cash.
the-rebound-is-a-calendar-not-a-verdict.text: Wall Street’s Monday was a partial undo of Friday’s AI-led drop. The S&P 500 rose about 0.5% in early trade; Nasdaq futures had been up about 1%; chip names led [1][2]. Lower oil and a softer tone in long Treasury yields helped [1][2]. None of that settles the question Friday posed: whether hyperscaler spending, expected by some houses near $1.2 trillion of combined capex next year, will throw off enough profit to justify the borrowing [2]. The week’s calendar is the print. Meta reports Wednesday; Tesla, Lam Research and Texas Instruments are also due; Netflix and GE Aerospace land Tuesday [2][3]. Swissquote’s Ipek Ozkardeskaya put the ask plainly: investors will want evidence that AI is generating revenue and profit, “not another ambitious spending plan” [2]. A rebound ahead of those dates is permitted. Treating it as proof is not. Wait for the cash-flow line.

meta-and-tesla-land-wednesday.title: Meta and Tesla land Wednesday
meta-and-tesla-land-wednesday.dek: Monday's AI bounce is a warm-up. The cash-flow lines later this week are the exam.
meta-and-tesla-land-wednesday.text: Meta reports Wednesday; Tesla, Lam Research and Texas Instruments are also on the week’s list; Netflix and GE Aerospace report Tuesday [1][2]. Hyperscaler capex chatter still circles figures near $1.2 trillion of combined spending next year in one Goldman estimate cited by Reuters [1]. Monday’s rebound does not settle whether that spending throws off cash. Wait for the free-cash-flow line and the guidance verbs.

campus-ai-rides-the-gulf-trip.title: Campus AI rides the Gulf trip
campus-ai-rides-the-gulf-trip.dek: Macron's UAE stop includes the president of a major AI hub near Paris that benefits from billions in Emirati funding.
campus-ai-rides-the-gulf-trip.text: The National reported that the president of Campus AI, a major hub under construction near Paris with billions in UAE funding, is travelling with Macron, alongside TotalEnergies and Engie chiefs, toward a Franco-Emirati business summit heavy on AI and energy [1]. Compute clusters need capital and power. Diplomatic trips are one place those invoices get discussed. Prefer signed capacity and interconnection dates to summit adjectives.

ecdc-monday-tally-eight-provinces.title: ECDC's Monday tally: eight provinces, and the follow-up rate still short
ecdc-monday-tally-eight-provinces.dek: As of 18 October the European centre counted 9,455 confirmed Bundibugyo cases and 4,561 deaths in Congo, with Nord Ubangi newly listed. Contact follow-up remains the dull lever that decides the map.
ecdc-monday-tally-eight-provinces.text: ECDC refreshed its Congo Bundibugyo page on Monday afternoon [1]. As of 18 October (data to 17 October) it reported 9,455 confirmed cases and 4,561 related deaths; 925 patients hospitalised in isolation; 2,530 recoveries among those who tested positive [1]. Since the previous ECDC update on 16 October (data to 14 October), an additional 178 confirmed cases and 83 deaths had been recorded [1]. Nord Ubangi is now listed: two confirmed cases from Wapinda health zone, bringing affected provinces to eight [1]. Ituri remains by far the heaviest burden (6,918 cases); 66 of 178 health zones across the eight provinces are affected [1]. About 80% of identified case contacts were under follow-up [1] — still short of the response’s own 95% discipline that this morning’s edition underlined from Congo’s SitRep. The constructive habit is unchanged: watch the follow-up rate and the laboratory throughput, not only the shaded map. An eighth province is serious. A contact seen today is how a ninth is avoided.

one-hundred-seventy-eight-cases-since-th.title: 178 cases since the last ECDC note
one-hundred-seventy-eight-cases-since-th.dek: Between the 16 October and 19 October updates, Congo's confirmed tally rose by 178 cases and 83 deaths.
one-hundred-seventy-eight-cases-since-th.text: ECDC’s Monday page states that since its 16 October update (data to 14 October), an additional 178 confirmed cases and 83 deaths were reported [1]. The cumulative print as of 18 October: 9,455 confirmed cases, 4,561 deaths, 925 in isolation, 2,530 recoveries among positives [1]. Pace matters as much as the stock. A weekday refresh that keeps showing triple-digit case increments is the opposite of a contained week.

nord-ubangi-two-cases-eighth-province.title: Nord Ubangi: two cases, eighth province
nord-ubangi-two-cases-eighth-province.dek: Wapinda health zone put a new province on ECDC's list. Small counts are how maps grow if follow-up slips.
nord-ubangi-two-cases-eighth-province.text: Two confirmed cases from Wapinda in Nord Ubangi brought the number of affected Congolese provinces to eight on ECDC’s tally [1]. Sud Ubangi had already listed two cases; the northern neighbour is now on the same sheet [1]. Early, tiny counts are when contact follow-up either works or fails. Eighty percent of identified contacts under follow-up is progress and still short of a 95% operational target [1].

milan-second-night-two-hundred-detained.title: Milan's second night: more than 200 detained
milan-second-night-two-hundred-detained.dek: Cost-of-living clashes in northern Italy produced a second day of looting and a government security summit.
milan-second-night-two-hundred-detained.text: France was not the only European capital of broken glass this weekend. In Milan, a second day of cost-of-living unrest brought fresh looting and more than 200 detentions, according to Euronews [1]. Turin and Bologna also saw clashes [1]. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence and convened a security meeting with police, carabinieri and intelligence chiefs on Monday [2]. The constructive comparison is institutional, not theatrical. Different countries, different interior ministries, the same demand: a public tally of arrests, injuries and shops, plus a dated plan for the next night. France published curfew instructions; Italy published a summit. Both are machinery. Neither is a slogan.

the-curfew-notices-were-posted.title: The curfew notices were posted — with hours, streets and ages
the-curfew-notices-were-posted.dek: This afternoon the curfews were a promise. By the evening they were orders: Paris from 23:00, the Nord from 20:00, Nice from 21:00.
the-curfew-notices-were-posted.text: This evening’s lead asked whether the curfew notices would appear with clear hours. They did. The Paris police prefecture said a curfew order runs from 23:00 on Monday to 06:00 on Tuesday on the esplanade of the Place de la République and the streets that lead into Les Halles from the south [1]. Demonstrations are also banned in some Paris districts from 20:00 to 06:00 [1][2]. In the Nord, the zone prefect signed an order covering minors in Lille, Douai, Wattignies and Denain from 20:00 to 06:00 for the next two nights [1]. In Nice, the mayor’s order keeps minors off central streets from 21:00 to 06:00 until Sunday [1][2]. Denain’s mayor narrowed her own Sunday order, which had covered the whole town of about 20,000 people, to parts of the centre and to unaccompanied minors only [2]. Look at what the paperwork shows. These are small orders, limited by hour, street and age, and each has an end date. That is what makes them checkable. Tomorrow’s tally of arrests and damaged shops in those streets, compared with the weekend, is the real test of whether they worked.

marseille-banned-the-gathering-for-a-day.title: Marseille banned the gathering for a day
marseille-banned-the-gathering-for-a-day.dek: Before national curfew talk, the southern port used the prefect's older tool: a temporary ban on public assemblies.
marseille-banned-the-gathering-for-a-day.text: Some cities, including Marseille, imposed a ban on public gatherings for most of Monday, NBC News reported [1]. That is narrower than a curfew and older in French administrative practice: a prefectural order with a clock on it. Lecornu later asked for localized curfews elsewhere while rejecting a blanket Paris curfew [1]. Watch which tool each prefecture actually posts tonight — ban, curfew, or neither — and for how many hours.

gard-and-herault-are-orange.title: Gard and Hérault are orange — Tuesday's list is longer
gard-and-herault-are-orange.dek: Météo-France's 16:04 vigilance put three departments in orange today and eight tomorrow. Cumuls of 200–300 mm are the print; the advice is still: do not drive into water.
gard-and-herault-are-orange.text: At 16:04 Paris time on Monday, Météo-France’s accessible vigilance listed Gard and Hérault in orange for rain-flood, storms and river rises, and Lozère in orange for rain-flood; thirteen departments were yellow [1]. For Tuesday the orange list lengthens to eight: Ardèche, Bouches-du-Rhône, Haute-Corse, Gard, Hérault, Lozère, Var and Vaucluse [1]. The agency’s episode note expects intense thunderstorm rains from Monday into Tuesday, with possible hourly totals of 60–80 mm, gusts to 80 km/h, hail and strong lightning, and episode cumuls of order 200–250 mm, locally 300 mm, on eastern Hérault and the Gard [2]. On Tuesday the rains shift east toward Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur and Corsica [2]. This is not a metaphor for climate politics. It is a public timetable: stay off submerged roads, avoid underpasses, follow prefecture instructions [2]. The constructive act tonight is local and dull — check the vigilance map before a journey, not after.

tuesday-eight-departments-in-orange.title: Tuesday: eight departments in orange
tuesday-eight-departments-in-orange.dek: Monday's three orange départements become eight as the Mediterranean episode shifts east.
tuesday-eight-departments-in-orange.text: Météo-France’s 16:04 Monday bulletin listed Gard, Hérault and Lozère in orange for Monday, then eight départements for Tuesday: Ardèche, Bouches-du-Rhône, Haute-Corse, Gard, Hérault, Lozère, Var and Vaucluse [1]. That is the episode moving, not ending. The constructive check is the next 06:00 and 16:00 updates — and whether your route crosses an orange cell before you drive.

two-hundred-to-three-hundred-millimetres.title: Two hundred to three hundred millimetres
two-hundred-to-three-hundred-millimetres.dek: Météo-France's episode note puts cumuls of 200–250 mm, locally 300 mm, on eastern Hérault and the Gard.
two-hundred-to-three-hundred-millimetres.text: Across the whole episode, expected cumuls on eastern Hérault and the Gard are of order 200–250 mm, locally 300 mm, on coast, plain and relief alike [1]. Hourly bursts of 60–80 mm are possible with gusts to 80 km/h [1]. Those figures are why orange exists. Stay out of underpasses; do not drive into water; follow the prefecture [1]. Rain totals are the weather’s ledger. Behaviour is yours.
